name: 3code
description: Open-source single-binary command-line coding agent by Carlo Capocasa, focused on token economy (chunked mode, goal files) and built-in sandboxing.

name: Aider
description: Open-source AI pair-programming tool for the terminal that edits code in a git repo using many model providers.

name: Amp
description: Agentic coding tool from Amp (spun out of Sourcegraph), available as a CLI and editor extension, with cloud runners.

name: Antigravity
description: Google's agent-first IDE/development platform (often abbreviated AGY) built around Gemini models, with an agent manager for running multiple agents.

name: Belfry
description: Open-source native macOS/iOS front-end for tmux showing hosts, sessions and windows in a sidebar with the live terminal, locally or over SSH; by Rob Gough.

name: Briefkin
description: Hosted dashboard and notification service where coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, scripts) report progress and blockers to a card board, with Telegram alerts when input is needed; in open beta.

name: Circus Chief
description: Open-source meta-harness for orchestrating Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Gemini CLI agents, with subscription fallback tiers; published on npm.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for Claude models, available as a terminal CLI, IDE extensions, a desktop app and on the web.

name: Claude Cowork
description: Claude Cowork, Anthropic's agent mode in the Claude desktop app (launched January 2026) that works on local files and connected apps to complete non-coding tasks.

name: Claude Desktop
description: Anthropic's Claude desktop app (macOS/Windows) with MCP connectors, used by the commenter as an agent platform.

name: Cline
description: Open-source autonomous coding agent, mainly used as a VS Code extension, also available as a CLI and SDK; bring-your-own model.

name: CodeBuddy
description: Tencent's AI coding assistant, offered as an IDE, editor plugins and CLI with free and Pro tiers and access to multiple models.

name: Codealong
description: Free, open-source macOS/Linux app that shows every coding agent you run (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, Cursor) in one window across accounts and machines.

name: Codex
description: OpenAI's coding agent, offered as an open-source terminal CLI plus IDE extension, desktop app and cloud agent, used with OpenAI models via ChatGPT plans or API.

name: Collie
description: Open-source iOS app for remotely controlling Herdr-managed coding agents (used over Tailscale).

name: Comet
description: Comet, Perplexity's AI-powered web browser with a built-in agent that can browse and act on websites for the user.

name: Conductor
description: Mac app for running parallel Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agents in isolated git-worktree workspaces and reviewing/merging their changes, by Melty Labs.

name: Contextify
description: macOS companion app for Claude Code and Codex CLI that monitors coding sessions with a timeline and LLM summaries, letting past session context be reused.

name: Corgi
description: Open-source terminal multiplexer/agent manager built on Ghostty and inspired by herdr, for running Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode sessions.

name: CrewAI
description: Open-source Python framework (and commercial platform) for orchestrating role-playing autonomous AI agents that collaborate on tasks.

name: Ctlflow
description: System for running a self-defined fleet of AI agents locally that people talk to through Matrix chat rooms, with a server (crossfire), local controller (fleetd) and CLI (fleet).

name: Cursor
description: Proprietary AI code editor (VS Code fork) with built-in agents, plus a Cursor CLI and cloud agents, sold by subscription by Anysphere.

name: DeepSeek Harness
description: DeepSeek's open-source (MIT) coding agent harness 'dsh', where every component is a plugin; runs as a CLI, web UI or headless and is used mainly with DeepSeek models. Released August 2026.

name: DeepSeek Superagent
description: DeepSeek's open-source research prototype of an autonomous Router/Worker 'super-agent' built on DeepSeek Harness that responds to and fixes issues in a repository; published October 2026.

name: DevArch
description: Commercial layer for Claude Code that adds directives, agents, hooks and skills to enforce engineering discipline (quality gates, session continuity, ADRs), by David Cornelson; paid annual license.

name: Devin
description: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer, used through a web app (with IDE/desktop and Slack integrations).

name: Dirge
description: Minimal open-source Rust coding agent inspired by pi, opencode and maki, with role-based multi-provider routing, persistent memory and safeguards for cheaper models.

name: Dots
description: OpenAI's dots, always-on agents in ChatGPT (launched at DevDay, September 2026) that have their own cloud computer and memory, connect to your apps, and can own projects and multi-step tasks.

name: Duet
description: Claude Duet, Anthropic's proactive always-on agent app (research preview from October 2026, waitlist invitations for US Pro/Max users) that monitors connected apps and works on tasks in the background.

name: Emacs (gptel etc.)
description: Bucket for using Emacs as the AI/agent environment, via packages such as gptel (LLM client) and Editor Code Assistant (ECA, eca.dev).

name: FreeBuff
description: Free, ad-supported terminal coding agent from the Codebuff team (YC F24) using open models.

name: Gas Town
description: Steve Yegge's open-source multi-agent workspace manager for coordinating many Claude Code-style agents on a codebase.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal coding agent for Gemini models.

name: GitHub Copilot
description: GitHub's AI coding assistant, available as IDE extensions, the Copilot CLI and a cloud coding agent, with access to models from several labs via subscription.

name: Goose
description: Open-source, extensible AI agent with desktop app and CLI that works with any LLM; originally created by Block, now under the aaif-goose organization.

name: Grok CLI
description: Terminal coding agent for xAI's Grok models; most likely xAI's official Grok Build CLI (an unofficial open-source grok-cli by superagent-ai also exists).

name: Hangar
description: Open-source, self-hosted app that puts Claude Code, Codex, Pi, omp and Kimi Code agents in one place, on desktop and phone.

name: Hax
description: Minimalist open-source (MIT) terminal-native coding agent written in C by Oleksandr Chekhovskyi.

name: Herdr
description: Open-source runtime and workspace for running many coding agents: a native desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows) plus the original terminal multiplexer TUI, with per-pane agent status and a socket API; agents run in a local herdr-core server.

name: Hermes Agent
description: Open-source, self-improving general-purpose AI agent from Nous Research that builds skills and memory from use, runs from the terminal or messaging gateways, and works with many model providers.

name: JetBrains AI / Junie
description: JetBrains' AI Assistant and Junie coding agent integrated into JetBrains IDEs.

name: JetBrains Thinkrail
description: JetBrains incubator project: an open-source agentic IDE (desktop and mobile) built as a thin layer around the pi coding agent, with per-chat git worktrees and SPEC.md-based project memory.

name: Juggler
description: Open-source desktop/browser workbench for AI coding agents by Julian Storer (creator of JUCE), with tree-structured persistent sessions and a headless server for remote machines; vendor-neutral.

name: Kepler
description: GitKraken's agentic development environment that turns issues from trackers (Jira, Linear, GitHub etc.) into tasks run by ACP agents in worktrees, with a Kanban view.

name: Kilo Code
description: Open-source agentic coding extension for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs (plus CLI) from Kilo, with access to many models.

name: Kimi Code
description: Moonshot AI's open-source terminal coding agent (Kimi Code CLI, successor to Kimi CLI) for Kimi models.

name: Kiro
description: Amazon/AWS's agentic IDE and CLI centred on spec-driven development.

name: Kiro Crew
description: Open-source companion to Amazon's Kiro providing a persistent, self-improving workspace with background subagents, scheduled jobs and persistent memory that continues beyond one session.

name: LangGraph
description: LangChain's open-source framework for building stateful, graph-structured LLM agents and multi-agent workflows.

name: Letta
description: Letta (formerly MemGPT), an open-source platform and cloud service for building stateful agents with long-term memory.

name: LoopX
description: Open-source, local-first control plane and research workbench for long-running agent teams that span multiple sessions and runtimes.

name: Lyre
description: Lyre Studio's AI workspace for running coding agents across your own computers, with live app previews on phones; builds on Paseo's open-source code.

name: Maki
description: Open-source (MIT) Rust terminal coding agent by Tony Solomonik focused on low context usage (tree-sitter index, sandboxed code execution), extendable with Lua plugins; supports many providers and ACP.

name: MetaGPT
description: Open-source multi-agent framework that simulates a software company of LLM roles; from FoundationAgents/DeepWisdom.

name: MiMo Code
description: Xiaomi's open-source terminal coding agent (an OpenCode fork tuned for MiMo models), released June 2026.

name: Mistral Vibe
description: Mistral AI's minimal open-source terminal coding agent for Mistral (and other) models.

name: Munder Difflin
description: Open-source local multi-agent harness that runs an 'office' of Claude Code/Codex-style agents on your laptop or sandboxes using existing subscriptions.

name: Muse
description: Meta's Muse AI family: the Muse Spark/Glimmer models, the Muse personal agent app, and Muse Code, Meta's coding agent with monthly plans starting at $5/month. Commenters used it as a coding model/subscription and personal assistant.

name: Muse Code
description: Meta's terminal coding agent powered by its Muse Spark models, launched August 2026 with plans from $5/month.

name: Muster
description: Open-source native macOS workspace for AI coding agents built on libghostty, with real splits, agent state at a glance, local and SSH agents, and sessions that outlive the app.

name: NanoClaw
description: Lightweight open-source alternative to OpenClaw that runs agents in isolated containers on the Claude Agent SDK and connects to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other messengers.

name: NodeCode
description: Open-source self-modifying agent written in Common Lisp (SBCL) that runs as one long-lived process with a single 'evaluate Lisp' tool.

name: Open Agent Harness (OAH)
description: Open-source multi-agent development harness for macOS and Windows that coordinates Claude Code and Codex, with file leases and task history.

name: Open WebUI
description: Open-source, self-hostable web chat interface for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs, extensible with plugins.

name: OpenBot
description: Open-source, self-hosted platform for running a team of AI bots with tools, long-term memory and persistent inboxes in shared threads; created by GitHub user regnull as an open alternative to Grok Bot.

name: OpenChamber
description: Open-source fan-made desktop, web/PWA and VS Code interface for the OpenCode agent.

name: OpenClaw
description: Open-source, self-hosted personal AI agent (formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot) created by Peter Steinberger that connects chat apps like WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal to an LLM agent that can run tasks.

name: OpenCode
description: Open-source, provider-agnostic coding agent with a terminal UI plus desktop and web clients; also sells the OpenCode Go/Zen model subscriptions. Made by Anomaly (formerly SST).

name: OpenHands
description: Open-source AI software-development agent platform (formerly OpenDevin) with CLI, local GUI and cloud versions.

name: OpenRig
description: Open-source tool for building persistent teams of Claude Code, Codex and Pi agents with roles, shared context and owned work, running in tmux.

name: OpenSWE
description: Open SWE, LangChain's open-source framework for internal asynchronous coding agents, built on LangGraph/Deep Agents and invokable from Slack or GitHub to open PRs.

name: Orca
description: Open-source desktop app (with CLI and mobile companion) for running a fleet of coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in parallel terminals, each in its own git worktree. Made by Stably AI.

name: Ori
description: OpenRouter's family of agent tools: Ori Code, a native terminal coding agent, and Ori Harness, which runs existing agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) through OpenRouter models.

name: Osaurus
description: Osaurus, an open-source native macOS (Apple Silicon) app for running local and cloud AI models with agents, memory and tools on your Mac.

name: Paperclip
description: Open-source app for managing AI agents at work, coordinating multiple agents on tasks.

name: Paseo
description: Open-source, self-hosted daemon plus desktop, mobile, web and CLI clients for orchestrating multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and others) with worktrees and diff review.

name: Paseo / Orca / Superset
description: Group of 'harness aggregator' apps for running multiple coding agents in parallel: Paseo (desktop and mobile), Orca by Stably AI (desktop/mobile/remote, MIT) and Superset (superset.sh).

name: Pi
description: Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (pi / pi-mono) by Mario Zechner, with a small toolset, TypeScript extensions and support for many model providers; now hosted under Earendil Works.

name: Pickle
description: Likely Pickle (getpickle.ai), a startup offering AI clones/personal AI you can talk to, which the commenter uses to make calls while driving; exact product unverified.

name: Rakazo
description: Rakazo, an open-source (Apache 2.0) self-hosted platform for persistent AI bots that sign into your tools and complete tasks with sandboxed browser/shell, memory and routines; built by Inbox Zero as an open alternative to Grok Bot.

name: Raven
description: EverMind AI's open-source 'harness of harnesses' that plans tasks as a dependency graph and delegates nodes to its own agents or to third-party harnesses like Claude Code and Codex (via ACP/CLI/APIs); pre-alpha.

name: Rex
description: Combined native terminal emulator and multiplexer (built on libghostty) from Mitchell Hashimoto's company Superlogical, with built-in sessions, splits and persistence; macOS client in public testing since Oct 2026.

name: Scion
description: Google Cloud's experimental open-source orchestrator that runs multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex) in parallel, each in its own container with separate credentials and git worktree.

name: Swival
description: Small open-source (MIT) Python CLI coding agent aimed at open and local models, with memory, review loops, MCP and A2A support.

name: T3 Code
description: Open-source 'agent harness control surface' from T3 Tools (Theo Browne) - desktop (Electron), web and mobile apps that drive locally installed agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Antigravity.

name: Termic
description: Open-source (AGPL) Conductor.build alternative that runs the real Claude, Gemini and Codex CLIs in real terminals for switching between parallel agents.

name: VS Code
description: Microsoft's open-source code editor, used here as the host for AI agents (Copilot, Claude Code, Cline etc.) and extensions.

name: Volt
description: Open-source (MIT) fork of the Pi coding agent by Jordan Hans: a terminal coding agent with planning, code review, subagents, Pi-compatible extensions and an iOS companion.

name: Warp
description: Agentic development environment built around a modern terminal, with built-in agents, from Warp.

name: ZCode
description: Z.ai (Zhipu AI)'s desktop coding-agent app for its GLM models, used with the GLM Coding Plan.

name: Zed
description: Open-source, high-performance code editor written in Rust by Zed Industries, with built-in AI agent panel and support for external agents via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

name: ZeroStack
description: Lightweight open-source coding agent written in Rust by gi-dellav, optimized for low memory use, with multiple providers, prompt modes, worktrees and ACP support.

name: agent-swarm.dev
description: Agent Swarm: MIT-licensed, self-hostable multi-agent system where a lead agent delegates goals to worker agents such as Claude Code or Codex; a paid hosted cloud version also exists. By Desplega Labs.

name: agentcron.ai
description: AgentCron, a team collaboration workspace (chat, projects/kanban, docs, files) usable with AI agents such as ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, e.g. via MCP.

name: clawpatrol
description: Deno's open-source security firewall/proxy for AI agents that enforces action-approval rules and manages credentials.

name: cmux
description: Open-source Ghostty-based native macOS terminal for running multiple AI coding agents, with vertical workspace tabs, notifications when agents need input, and a CLI/socket API.

name: epiq
description: Open-source, Git-native distributed issue tracker and workflow manager for agentic teams, with a terminal UI and no server or account needed.

name: llm-desktop-electron
description: Small open-source Electron app by mkornreich for running a Claude Desktop-style chat UI with non-Claude models (e.g. via OpenRouter).

name: yaac
description: Open-source tool by the commenter that auto-containerizes coding agents (gVisor containers) and provides inter-agent orchestration.
